author: NASASpaceflight
description:
SpaceX has revealed the ambitious mission profile for Starship Flight 14—and if everything goes according to plan, Ship 41 will become the first Starship to enter orbit.

During a nearly 10-hour mission, Ship 41 is expected to complete approximately six orbits of Earth, deploy 26 operational Starlink V3 satellites and conduct a deorbit burn before splashing down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Chile. But Starship won’t commit to orbit immediately: SpaceX has designed an Indian Ocean fallback trajectory in case the vehicle isn’t healthy enough to perform its orbital insertion burn.

Flight 14 is now targeted for no earlier than September 28, pending regulatory approval from the FAA.

We break down the complete Flight 14 mission, including:

• Starship’s orbital insertion and contingency plans
• Deployment of the first operational Starlink V3 satellites
• Ship 41’s nine-hour orbital coast and deorbit burn
• Pacific splashdown plans
• Booster 21’s upgrades and planned Gulf splashdo
title: Starship’s Biggest Flight Yet: Flight 14 Mission Revealed | Starship Update

author: NASASpaceflight
description:
Join us as SpaceX rolls Ship 41 to Pad 2 ahead of Starship Flight 14. SpaceX is expected to go to Full Stack soon after.

B21 previously performed three cryogenic proofing tests on July 18th, 19th, and 20th. A scrub occurred before prop loading during Wednesday's test window.

Ship 41 has performed single-engine and six-engine static fires.
